    API Reference

    This reference is generated from the public Python API shipped in the SynthNova Docker image. PhysicsSimulator is a compatibility alias of MujocoSimulator. Source code is intentionally not embedded in the site.

    Simulator

    physics_simulator.simulator.mujoco.MujocoSimulator(physics_simulator_config: PhysicsSimulatorConfig)

    Bases: BaseSim

    High-level MuJoCo simulation runtime.

    The simulator owns the MuJoCo model and data, scene entities, sensors, render contexts, physics callbacks, and optional interactive viewer. Scene content can be supplied in :class:~synthnova_config.PhysicsSimulatorConfig or added before :meth:initialize.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    physics_simulator_config PhysicsSimulatorConfig

    Validated simulator, logging, and scene configuration.

    		 required
    Note

    physics_simulator.PhysicsSimulator is a compatibility alias for this class.

    Initialize the MuJoCo-based physics simulator.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    physics_simulator_config PhysicsSimulatorConfig

    Configuration object containing all simulator settings

    		 required

    Attributes

    root_directory instance-attribute

    synthnova_assets_directory instance-attribute

    root_prim_path instance-attribute

    config instance-attribute

    model instance-attribute

    data instance-attribute

    viewer instance-attribute

    lock instance-attribute

    logger instance-attribute

    world instance-attribute

    Methods:

    load_model_from_xml_string(xml)

    Load a MuJoCo model from an XML string.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    xml

    String containing MuJoCo model XML

    		 required

    load_model_from_xml_path(xml_file)

    Load a MuJoCo model from an XML file.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    xml_file

    Path to the XML file

    		 required

    initialize()

    Initialize the simulator by setting up the MuJoCo model, data structures, and viewer. Must be called before stepping the simulation.

    forward()

    Run forward dynamics to synchronize derived quantities in MuJoCo. This updates all computed quantities in the simulation without advancing time.

    step(num_steps: int = 1, physics: bool = True, render: bool = True)

    Step simulation and execute physics callbacks.

    step1(num_steps: int = 1)

    Execute the first part of simulation steps (before control inputs). This computes forward dynamics without integrating positions.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    num_steps int

    Number of simulation step1 operations to execute

    		 1

    step2(num_steps: int = 1, render: bool = True)

    Execute the second part of simulation steps (after control inputs). This integrates positions and updates the simulation state.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    num_steps int

    Number of simulation step2 operations to execute

    		 1
    render bool

    Whether to update viewer after stepping

    		 True

    render(width=None, height=None, *, camera_name=None, depth=False, mode='offscreen', device_id=-1, segmentation=False)

    Render the current scene from a specific camera view.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    width

    Image width in pixels

    		 None
    height

    Image height in pixels

    		 None
    camera_name

    Name of the camera to render from

    		 None
    depth

    Whether to render depth information

    		 False
    mode

    Rendering mode ('offscreen' or 'window')

    		 'offscreen'
    device_id

    GPU device ID to use for rendering

    		 -1
    segmentation

    Whether to render segmentation mask

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description

    numpy.ndarray: The rendered image

    add_render_context(render_context)

    is_running() -> bool

    Check if the simulator is initialized and running.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    bool bool

    True if the simulator is running, False otherwise

    play()

    Start the simulation if it's not already running.

    loop(ctrl_dt: float = 0.004, render_dt: float = 0.04)

    Run the simulation loop.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    ctrl_dt float

    Control cycle duration in seconds. Physics steps per cycle are derived from simulator timestep.

    		 0.004
    render_dt float

    Minimum wall-clock interval between viewer refreshes (ignored when headless).

    		 0.04

    run_loop_thread(ctrl_dt: float = 0.004, render_dt: float = 0.04, daemon: bool = True)

    Start the simulation loop in a background thread.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    ctrl_dt float

    Control cycle duration in seconds.

    		 0.004
    render_dt float

    Viewer refresh interval in seconds (ignored when headless).

    		 0.04
    daemon bool

    Whether the thread should be daemon.

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description

    threading.Thread: The started thread (or existing running one).

    reset()

    Reset the simulation to its initial state.

    close()

    Clean up and close the simulator, releasing all resources.

    free()

    Clean up resources and prevent memory leaks.

    get_scene_config(*, scene_name: str | None = None, scene_description: str | None = None, to_relative_paths: bool = False) -> SceneConfig

    CustomMaterial(texture, tex_name, mat_name, tex_attrib=None, mat_attrib=None, shared=False)

    Simple class to instantiate the necessary parameters to define an appropriate texture / material combo

    Instantiates a nested dict holding necessary components for procedurally generating a texture / material combo

    Please see http://www.mujoco.org/book/XMLreference.html#asset for specific details on attributes expected for Mujoco texture / material tags, respectively

    Note that the values in @tex_attrib and @mat_attrib can be in string or array / numerical form.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    texture None or str or 4 - array

    Name of texture file to be imported. If a string, should be part of ALL_TEXTURES. If texture is a 4-array, then this argument will be interpreted as an rgba tuple value and a template png will be procedurally generated during object instantiation, with any additional texture / material attributes specified. If None, no file will be linked and no rgba value will be set Note, if specified, the RGBA values are expected to be floats between 0 and 1

    		 required
    tex_name str

    Name to reference the imported texture

    		 required
    mat_name str

    Name to reference the imported material

    		 required
    tex_attrib dict

    Any other optional mujoco texture specifications.

    		 None
    mat_attrib dict

    Any other optional mujoco material specifications.

    		 None
    shared bool

    If True, this material should not have any naming prefixes added to all names

    		 False

    Type Description

    		 None
    solref 2-tuple of float

    MuJoCo solver parameters that handle contact. See http://www.mujoco.org/book/XMLreference.html for more details.

    MuJoCo solver parameters that handle contact. See http://www.mujoco.org/book/XMLreference.html for more details.

    		 None

    if "default", add a template material and texture for this object that is used to color the geom(s). Otherwise, input is expected to be a CustomMaterial object

    See http://www.mujoco.org/book/XMLreference.html#asset for specific details on attributes expected for Mujoco texture / material tags, respectively

    Note that specifying a custom texture in this way automatically overrides any rgba values set

    		 None
    joints None or str or list of dict

    Joints for this object. If None, no joint will be created. If "default", a single (free) joint will be crated. Else, should be a list of dict, where each dictionary corresponds to a joint that will be created for this object.     		 'default'

    If set, will guarantee that each collision geom has a visual geom copy

    modify_xml_for_camera_movement(xml, camera_name)

    Cameras in mujoco are 'fixed', so they can't be moved by default. Although it's possible to hack position movement, rotation movement does not work. An alternative is to attach a camera to a mocap body, and move the mocap body.

    This function modifies the camera with name @camera_name in the xml by attaching it to a mocap body that can move around freely. In this way, we can move the camera by moving the mocap body.

    See http://www.mujoco.org/forum/index.php?threads/move-camera.2201/ for further details.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    xml str

    Mujoco sim XML file as a string

    		 required
    camera_name str

    Name of camera to tune

    		 required

    quat_slerp(quat0, quat1, fraction, shortestpath=True)

    Return spherical linear interpolation between two quaternions.

    E.g.:

    q0 = random_quat() q1 = random_quat() q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 0.0) np.allclose(q, q0) True

    q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 1.0) np.allclose(q, q1) True

    q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 0.5) angle = math.acos(np.dot(q0, q)) np.allclose(2.0, math.acos(np.dot(q0, q1)) / angle) or np.allclose(2.0, math.acos(-np.dot(q0, q1)) / angle) True

    rotation_matrix(angle, direction, point=None)

    Returns matrix to rotate about axis defined by point and direction.

    E.g.: >>> angle = (random.random() - 0.5) * (2math.pi) >>> direc = numpy.random.random(3) - 0.5 >>> point = numpy.random.random(3) - 0.5 >>> R0 = rotation_matrix(angle, direc, point) >>> R1 = rotation_matrix(angle-2math.pi, direc, point) >>> is_same_transform(R0, R1) True

    >>> R0 = rotation_matrix(angle, direc, point)
>>> R1 = rotation_matrix(-angle, -direc, point)
>>> is_same_transform(R0, R1)
True

>>> I = numpy.identity(4, numpy.float32)
>>> numpy.allclose(I, rotation_matrix(math.pi*2, direc))
True

>>> numpy.allclose(2., numpy.trace(rotation_matrix(math.pi/2,
...                                                direc, point)))
True

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default

    E.g.: >>> v0 = numpy.random.random(3) >>> v1 = unit_vector(v0) >>> numpy.allclose(v1, v0 / numpy.linalg.norm(v0)) True

    >>> v0 = numpy.random.rand(5, 4, 3)
>>> v1 = unit_vector(v0, axis=-1)
>>> v2 = v0 / numpy.expand_dims(numpy.sqrt(numpy.sum(v0*v0, axis=2)), 2)
>>> numpy.allclose(v1, v2)
True

>>> v1 = unit_vector(v0, axis=1)
>>> v2 = v0 / numpy.expand_dims(numpy.sqrt(numpy.sum(v0*v0, axis=1)), 1)
>>> numpy.allclose(v1, v2)
True

>>> v1 = numpy.empty((5, 4, 3), dtype=numpy.float32)
>>> unit_vector(v0, axis=1, out=v1)
>>> numpy.allclose(v1, v2)
True

>>> list(unit_vector([]))
[]

>>> list(unit_vector([1.0]))
[1.0]

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    data array

    data to normalize

    		 required
    axis None or int

    If specified, determines specific axis along data to normalize

    		 None
    out None or array

    If specified, will store computation in this variable

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description

    None or np.array: If @out is not specified, will return normalized vector. Otherwise, stores the output in @out

    quat_slerp(quat0, quat1, fraction, shortestpath=True)

    Return spherical linear interpolation between two quaternions.

    E.g.:

    q0 = random_quat() q1 = random_quat() q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 0.0) np.allclose(q, q0) True

    q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 1.0) np.allclose(q, q1) True

    q = quat_slerp(q0, q1, 0.5) angle = math.acos(np.dot(q0, q)) np.allclose(2.0, math.acos(np.dot(q0, q1)) / angle) or np.allclose(2.0, math.acos(-np.dot(q0, q1)) / angle) True

    rotation_matrix(angle, direction, point=None)

    Returns matrix to rotate about axis defined by point and direction.

    E.g.: >>> angle = (random.random() - 0.5) * (2math.pi) >>> direc = numpy.random.random(3) - 0.5 >>> point = numpy.random.random(3) - 0.5 >>> R0 = rotation_matrix(angle, direc, point) >>> R1 = rotation_matrix(angle-2math.pi, direc, point) >>> is_same_transform(R0, R1) True

    >>> R0 = rotation_matrix(angle, direc, point)
>>> R1 = rotation_matrix(-angle, -direc, point)
>>> is_same_transform(R0, R1)
True

>>> I = numpy.identity(4, numpy.float32)
>>> numpy.allclose(I, rotation_matrix(math.pi*2, direc))
True

>>> numpy.allclose(2., numpy.trace(rotation_matrix(math.pi/2,
...                                                direc, point)))
True

    CustomMaterial(texture, tex_name, mat_name, tex_attrib=None, mat_attrib=None, shared=False)

    Simple class to instantiate the necessary parameters to define an appropriate texture / material combo

    Instantiates a nested dict holding necessary components for procedurally generating a texture / material combo

    Please see http://www.mujoco.org/book/XMLreference.html#asset for specific details on attributes expected for Mujoco texture / material tags, respectively

    Note that the values in @tex_attrib and @mat_attrib can be in string or array / numerical form.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    texture None or str or 4 - array

    Name of texture file to be imported. If a string, should be part of ALL_TEXTURES. If texture is a 4-array, then this argument will be interpreted as an rgba tuple value and a template png will be procedurally generated during object instantiation, with any additional texture / material attributes specified. If None, no file will be linked and no rgba value will be set Note, if specified, the RGBA values are expected to be floats between 0 and 1

    		 required
    tex_name str

    Name to reference the imported texture

    		 required
    mat_name str

    Name to reference the imported material

    		 required
    tex_attrib dict

    Any other optional mujoco texture specifications.

    		 None
    mat_attrib dict

    Any other optional mujoco material specifications.

    		 None
    shared bool

    If True, this material should not have any naming prefixes added to all names

    		 False

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AssertionError

    [Invalid texture]

    physics_simulator.utils.threading_utils

    Threading utilities for physics simulator.

    This module provides thread-safe utilities and context managers for managing concurrent access to simulation resources.

    Attributes

    DEFAULT_THREAD_TIMEOUT module-attribute

    physics_simulator.utils.errors

    Classes

    PhysicsSimulatorError

    Bases: Exception

    Base exception class for all errors in the Physics Simulator.

    All custom exceptions in the physics simulator package should inherit from this class to enable proper error handling and categorization.

    XMLError

    Bases: PhysicsSimulatorError

    Exception raised for errors related to XML processing.

    This exception is raised when there are issues with parsing, validating, or manipulating XML files used for model definitions, configurations, etc.

    SimulationError

    Bases: PhysicsSimulatorError

    Exception raised for errors occurring during simulation runtime.

    This includes physics calculation errors, state inconsistencies, or other issues that prevent the simulation from progressing correctly.

    RandomizationError

    Bases: PhysicsSimulatorError

    Exception raised for errors in randomization processes.

    This can occur when random number generation fails or produces values that would create an invalid simulation state.
